text:
Vegas won 5-2 in Nashville, but the Predators were the team that played the better game. Nashville fired 60 shot attempts to Vegas's 45, finished with the higher expected goals total (2.37 to 2.08), and won 56 percent of simulated replays of every shot. The gap came from finishing. Vegas scored on chances that were rated between 1 and 14 percent, while Juuse Saros stopped nearly three goals fewer than the shots against him should have allowed (minus 2.92).

The first period set the pattern. Ryan O'Reilly gave Nashville the lead 3:55 in on a backhand, a 21 percent chance, the best look of any goal in the game. Tomas Hertl answered on an 11 percent wrist shot, and Jack Eichel tipped in an 8 percent chance to put Vegas up 2-1 even though Nashville held the edge in chance quality that period (1.05 to 0.72). Adam Edstrom tied it 2-2 on a shorthanded wrist shot in the second, but William Karlsson restored the lead with 16 seconds short of the period's end on an 11 percent snap shot.

The game ended in a 94-second burst early in the third. Trevor Connelly made it 4-2 at 4:49 with a wrist shot, and Brett Howden tipped in a 1 percent chance at 6:24 for the fifth goal. Adin Hill needed only to be solid, and he was, stopping 23 of 25 against an expected 2.37 goals. Filip Forsberg put seven shots on goal for Nashville and got a single assist for his work. Vegas took the points by turning modest chances into goals, and Nashville had little to show for the better play.
